title: Set C — poisoned input, a near-identically named different entity

questions.question: When was Marrow Lane Press founded?
questions.plantedFact: All four genuine sources say 2009. The impostor (set-c-05) says 1986, so a run that merges it produces a disputed founding-date group — 2009 against 1986 — where the correct answer is an agreed group at 2009 with the impostor excluded entirely. That specific wrong output is the failure this case is built to catch, and it is the demo moment: the model must decline to reconcile two entities that merely share a name.

questions.question: Where is the press based?
questions.plantedFact: Kelmore in all four genuine sources; set-c-03 narrows it to two rooms above a bakery. The impostor is in Tarnbridge, so a merged run yields a bogus Kelmore-versus-Tarnbridge dispute.

questions.question: How many books does the press publish each year?
questions.plantedFact: Six titles a year, phrased as "around six titles a year", "six or so books a year", "Six titles a year", and "three of this year's six titles". The impostor states no title count at all — it prints for clients and says it does not publish under its own imprint — so there is nothing here to conflict with, only something to wrongly import.

questions.question: What prize does the press run?
questions.plantedFact: The Kelmore Pamphlet Prize, in all four genuine sources. set-c-02 calls it simply "its pamphlet prize", which is the same prize under a shorter name rather than a second one.

notes: Expected outcome: four agreed groups, zero disputed, and not one claim citing set-c-05. The impostor is a commercial printer in Tarnbridge called Marrowlane Press Ltd — one space and one suffix away from the real subject, with shared vocabulary (press, printing, founded) to make name-similarity matching look reasonable. The disambiguating signal is available to a careful reader: it prints packaging and labels for clients and explicitly does not publish under its own imprint, so it cannot be the poetry publisher the other four sources describe. Any claim citing set-c-05 is a test failure, however plausible the claim itself sounds.
